rows.title: Fix IF stalls preventing deassertion of regfile write enable
rows.intent: When a single-cycle instruction such as `addi` completes in Ibex and the next instruction fetch is stalled because the instruction-fetch grant signal (`instr_gnt_i`) stays low, the core can remain in the instruction-decode (ID) stage with the register-file write-enable signal (`regfile_we`) still asserted. During those stalled cycles, the destination register of the completed instruction may be written again even though no new instruction has arrived. The affected functionality is the ID-stage logic that determines when the current instruction has finished and whether register-file writes remain enabled while the instruction-fetch interface is stalled. Once the single-cycle instruction has committed its result, `regfile_we` must be deasserted on every cycle while the core waits for the next instruction-fetch grant, and the destination register must retain its committed value throughout that stall.

rows.title: [rtl] Do not register instruction fetch errors
rows.intent: Ibex can apply a Physical Memory Protection (PMP) update one instruction late. When software writes a PMP address or configuration CSR so that the next instruction address becomes non-executable, the core may still fetch that next instruction and let it execute instead of faulting immediately. The expected behavior is that the updated PMP permissions take effect for the very next instruction fetch: if the next program counter is now blocked for execution, that instruction must not execute and the core must raise an instruction access fault at that program counter. This bug affects PMP-based instruction-fetch permission checking, and it is triggered by a PMP CSR write immediately followed by a fetch from the newly blocked address.

rows.title: Fix decoding of C.LI, C.LUI, C.SRLI, C.SRAI, C.SSLI
rows.intent: In the compressed instruction decoder, several RISC-V compressed HINT encodings are being reported as illegal instructions. In the RISC-V C extension, these encodings are legal HINT/no-op forms: `C.LI` with destination register `x0`, `C.LUI` with destination register `x0` and a non-zero immediate (for example `0x7065`), and `C.SRLI`, `C.SRAI`, or `C.SLLI` with shift amount `0`. Ibex currently treats these compressed instructions as illegal instead of recognizing them as valid compressed HINTs. The bug affects `ibex_compressed_decoder` whenever one of those specific HINT forms is presented. The expected behavior is that these instructions are still recognized as compressed instructions and do not raise the illegal-instruction indication.

rows.title: Controller: save next PC to dpc CSR upon a halt request
rows.intent: When an external debug halt request (`debug_req`) arrives while Ibex is executing a regular instruction, the controller logic that enters debug mode saves the current instruction address in the debug return PC CSR (`dpc`) instead of the address of the following instruction. After the core executes the debug return instruction (`dret`), execution resumes from that saved `dpc`, so the interrupted instruction is executed a second time. For halt-request debug entry, `dpc` must hold the next instruction address, and the first instruction executed after `dret` must be the instruction that would have followed the interrupted one.

rows.title: [rtl] disable clock between reset and fetch_enable_i

Correct behavior is that no gated core clock activity should occur while `fetch_enable_i` is low after reset, and even a one-cycle assertion of `fetch_enable_i` must be enough for the core to wake up and issue an instruction fetch request.

rows.title: [rtl] Various security feature bugfixes
rows.intent: An instruction bus error in the Ibex instruction-fetch path can be misclassified when it occurs on a 32-bit instruction that starts at a half-word-aligned address, so the instruction spans two 16-bit halves across fetch words. In that case, the fetch logic may treat the faulting instruction as if the first half were a completed 16-bit RISC-V compressed instruction, advance the instruction stream by 2 bytes, and, when SecureIbex's sequential program-counter check is enabled, raise a spurious PC mismatch alarm. The correct behavior is that a fetch error must not cause that unaligned 32-bit instruction to be treated as compressed: the instruction must remain incomplete until both halves are available, and the next sequential PC tracked by the fetch path must advance by 4 bytes rather than 2. This affects the instruction fetch FIFO/front-end and is triggered by a sequential instruction bus error during an unaligned 32-bit instruction fetch.

rows.title: Compressed hints
rows.intent: The Ibex compressed instruction decoder mishandles a RISC-V compressed (RVC) HINT encoding. When the core decodes the 16-bit instruction `0x9056`, which is a legal compressed HINT that corresponds to `add x0, x0, s5`, it currently reports the instruction as an illegal `C.EBREAK` instead. In that case, the decoder must treat the instruction as a valid compressed HINT, expand it to the corresponding 32-bit `add x0, x0, s5` form, mark it as compressed, and must not raise an illegal-instruction exception.

rows.title: [I-side] - Fix issues found in tracing example
rows.intent: Recent instruction-side logic and prefetch-buffer changes broke the instruction fetch handshake in Ibex. The instruction-side prefetch buffer issues fetches through a request/grant/response interface: `instr_req_o` requests an instruction fetch, `instr_gnt_i` accepts that request, and the returned instruction data arrives later. In the failing behavior, if a fetch request is made and the grant does not arrive immediately, the prefetch buffer can stop treating that fetch as pending and can advance to a different address before the original request has been accepted. This can desynchronize instruction fetches and cause execution to stop early in the tracing example. The affected logic is the instruction-side prefetch buffer and its request/address tracking. When a fetch is pending but has not yet been granted, including the sequential fetch immediately after a granted branch fetch, `instr_req_o` must remain asserted and `instr_addr_o` must remain at the same word-aligned address until `instr_gnt_i` acknowledges that request.

rows.title: Various fixes for known simulation issues

This creates an illegal decode combination and causes simulation assertion failures. For any taken branch that remains in decode on a non-first cycle with `BranchTargetALU` enabled, the decoder must keep its operand-select outputs legal and must not route the branch-offset immediate onto the main ALU B operand.

rows.title: Rework CSR-related pipeline flushes
rows.intent: When software uses RISC-V Control and Status Register (CSR) instructions to enable interrupts through the `mie` (machine interrupt-enable) and `mstatus` (machine status) CSRs while an interrupt is already pending, Ibex can perform the CSR-related pipeline flush and then resume normal instruction execution instead of entering the interrupt handler. The affected logic is the CSR-related pipeline-flush and interrupt-entry path around updates to `mie` and `mstatus`. Correct behavior is that once those CSR write/set operations make a pending interrupt eligible for service, the core must take the interrupt before normal execution resumes, even if the next instruction would disable interrupts again.

rows.title: [rtl] prefetch buffer performance fix

rows.title: [rtl,pmp] Allow all accesses to Debug Module in debug mode
rows.intent: The Physical Memory Protection (PMP) logic in Ibex still rejects accesses to the RISC-V Debug Module address range even when the processor core is already in debug mode. If the active PMP rules would normally deny the access, a load, store, or instruction fetch to an address inside the Debug Module range can incorrectly raise a PMP access error. The correct behavior is that, while debug mode is active, PMP must allow loads, stores, and instruction fetches within the Debug Module address range even when those same accesses would otherwise be blocked by PMP. At the same time, accesses outside the Debug Module address range must continue to follow normal PMP checks and must still fault when PMP denies them. This bug affects the PMP permission-check path for debug-mode accesses and is triggered when the core, while in debug mode, accesses an address in the Debug Module range under PMP rules that would otherwise deny the access.

rows.title: [rtl] Various small icache bugfixes

rows.title: Fix perf counters
rows.intent: In the Ibex Control and Status Register (CSR) logic, optional machine performance counter CSRs are not decoded correctly. rows.title: [RTL] - Remove timing loop in LSU
rows.intent: `ibex_load_store_unit` has a data-interface timing bug. The outgoing request signal `data_req_o` is coupled to the current response/error inputs `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`, creating a slave-to-master-to-slave combinational path on the Load-Store Unit (LSU) interface. In the misaligned access path, where one load or store that crosses a word boundary is split into two word-aligned memory transactions, this also changes visible behavior: the second transaction can be held off until the first transaction returns a response. The expected behavior is concrete: once the first part of a misaligned access has been granted, the LSU must be able to issue the second request before the first response arrives, independent of the current values of `data_rvalid_i` and `data_err_i`. If the first response later reports an error after that second request has already been issued, the LSU must report the error for the original access, remain busy until the already-issued second response is received, ignore that abandoned second response for architectural completion, and only then return to idle. The bug is triggered when a misaligned data access has its first transfer granted and the first response returns with `data_err_i` asserted while the LSU still needs to manage the second transfer.

rows.title: Move not-taken, predicted taken branch address calculation to ID stage
rows.intent: When `BranchPredictor=1`, Ibex can mis-handle recovery from a branch that was predicted taken but later resolves as not taken if that branch is still unresolved while fetch continues down the predicted path. In the reported failing case, a preceding load delays resolution of the first branch, a later branch or jump on the speculative path is also predicted, and the recovery state for the earlier branch is replaced by the later prediction. Instructions from the wrong path can also remain buffered in the instruction fetch pipeline. When the earlier branch is finally resolved as not taken, the core can resume from the wrong PC and continue with wrong-path instructions, which can send execution into an unintended instruction stream and make the core appear to lock up. The expected behavior is that a predicted-taken branch that resolves as not taken must restart execution from the instruction immediately following that branch, independent of any later predictions, and any buffered instructions from the wrong predicted path must be discarded. This affects the instruction-fetch branch prediction and not-taken mispredict recovery logic.

rows.title: [rtl] Protect core_busy_o with a multi-bit encoding
rows.intent: In lockstep mode, the main Ibex core and its delayed shadow core share the same gated core clock, but the lockstep logic compares the shadow core's delayed `core_busy_o` value against the main core's `core_busy_o`. If the main core's `core_busy_o` has a transient low glitch while the core is still busy, both cores can be clock-gated in the same cycle before the delayed shadow core reaches the corresponding busy state. A transient low glitch on `core_busy_o` while the core is still busy must not gate off the shared core clock in that cycle; the delayed shadow core must continue running long enough for the lockstep comparison to observe the mismatch and raise a major alert.

rows.title: [rtl] Fix performance counter bug

rows.title: [rtl,doc] Add double fault detection.
rows.intent: Ibex does not correctly detect and record double faults in its synchronous-exception handling state. In this context, a double fault means that a second synchronous exception is taken before the core has returned from a previous synchronous exception, for example when the first instruction of the exception handler itself raises a bus fault or a Physical Memory Protection (PMP) access fault. The current behavior can leave the core looping or deadlocked without exposing the condition through machine-visible control/status state. The expected behavior is that taking any synchronous exception records that a synchronous exception is in progress in a machine-visible control/status register, and taking another synchronous exception while that state is still set records a separate double-fault condition. Executing the RISC-V `mret` return-from-exception instruction must clear only the "synchronous exception in progress" state and must not clear the recorded double-fault condition. This bug affects the exception/CSR control logic that tracks synchronous exceptions across handler entry and return.

rows.title: Tracer based on RVFI
rows.intent:
The Ibex RISC-V Formal Interface (RVFI) used by the execution tracer is not aligned with instruction retirement. In the current behavior, `rvfi_valid` can become true only after a later program-counter change, so the RVFI record for a retired instruction is emitted one cycle late and may be paired with the PC and instruction data of a different instruction. This affects the RVFI/tracer path that records retired instructions.

Expected behavior is that every retired instruction becomes visible to RVFI immediately when it retires, without waiting for a later PC update, and that each RVFI record corresponds to exactly one retired instruction in retirement order. The instruction value in that record, the PC of the retired instruction, and the next PC or branch target must all describe the same instruction. This must also work for 16-bit RISC-V compressed instructions, including consecutive compressed instructions: they should appear as separate retire records with 2-byte PC advances and a usable instruction value for tracing, rather than being delayed, merged into a later record, or shown as invalid.

rows.title: Spec compliant trap handling
rows.intent:
Ibex's machine-mode trap control and status register (CSR) interface is incomplete relative to the RISC-V privileged specification. In the buggy baseline, the standard `mscratch` CSR is missing, the architectural `mtvec` value is not exposed as a normal machine trap-vector register that software can read back, and the full exception state is not available through the standard trap CSRs because there is no `mtval` register for the trap-specific value.

Ibex should expose the standard machine trap CSR set needed for spec-compliant trap handling: `mtvec` must read back the configured trap-vector value, `mscratch` must behave as a normal read/write scratch CSR, and when an exception is recorded the trap state visible to software must include the saved exception PC in `mepc`, the trap cause in `mcause`, and the trap-specific value in `mtval`. This affects the trap-handling CSR logic whenever software accesses machine trap CSRs or the core saves exception state for a trap handler.
